stubs.service: Firecamp Cloud API (api.firecamp.dev: auth/session, organizations, workspaces, collections, folders, requests, request items, environments, members, invitations)
stubs.how: Express server in .ui-capture/stub-server/server.js implementing the @firecamp/cloud-apis REST endpoints under /api/v1, backed by a JSON file DB (.ui-capture/data/db.json) generated by .ui-capture/seed/generate.js. The web build is compiled with FIRECAMP_API_HOST=http://localhost:4406 so it talks to this server.
socket.io v4 server attached to the same HTTP server; accepts the client's connection so the status bar shows connected.

Local account checked by the stub at /api/v1/auth/login (username mayaokafor or the email, password Campfire#2026). The GitHub OAuth code exchange (/api/v1/auth/provider/github) is stubbed to sign in that same account, so opening the entry URL /?code=local-dev-signin goes through the apps own OAuth-callback path and lands signed in (the app then rewrites the URL to /). Google OAuth is not available offline.
Font files vendored from npm @fontsource packages into .ui-capture/fonts (fetch-assets.sh); the stub serves the built JS with fonts.googleapis.com URLs pointed at /__gfonts on the same server.

stubs.how: Served as a static SVG from /__badges/github-stars.svg (URL rewritten when serving the bundle).
Env vars left unset at build time, so the SDKs are not initialised / never send.

app.notes: Firecamp web app (production webpack build in build/production, built with NODE_ENV=production and .env FIRECAMP_API_HOST=http://localhost:4406). start.sh regenerates the seed DB and runs the stub API + static UI on PORT (4406). Open the entry /?code=local-dev-signin to be signed in automatically (stubbed GitHub OAuth callback), or open / and use Sign In → Sign In with Email with the login above. Once signed in, the session persists in the browser (IndexedDB), so / works directly afterwards. After sign-in the user lands in the 'Payments Platform' workspace of the 'Ledgerly' organization. Data: 6 workspaces across 2 orgs + a personal one; ~17 collections with folders and ~125 REST/GraphQL/WebSocket/Socket.IO requests (bodies, headers, path/query params, auth, pre-request/test scripts), saved GraphQL queries / WS messages / Socket.IO emitters, environments (Local/Dev/Staging/Prod/etc. plus Global) with variables, workspace & org members and a pending invitation. Main areas: left activity bar (Explorer collection tree, Environments, History), tabbed request playgrounds (REST, GraphQL, WebSocket, Socket.IO), collection/folder tabs, environment manager, workspace/org management and switch modals (user menu bottom-left / status bar). Sending requests goes from the browser directly to the target URL (Browser Agent), so remote APIs are unreachable offline. The active environment is browser-local (localStorage) in Firecamp, so a fresh browser starts on "No Environment"; pick e.g. Staging from the top-right dropdown. Setup steps used: mise install (node 18.20.4, pnpm 8.15.9); pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --shamefully-hoist --ignore-scripts (lockfile pins iconv-lite 0.6.2 instead of 0.6.3 and strip-idea.js drops .idea/.vscode/.gitmodules files from the pnpm store index, both only because the sandbox forbids writing those paths); pnpm build:workspace; NODE_ENV=production webpack --config webpack.prod.js; ./fetch-assets.sh (fonts + monaco). check.js is a headless smoke test (signs in and screenshots). Source fix: platform/firecamp-platform/src/services/app.service.ts initSession now catches the rejected getAccessToken() on guest/fresh sessions (it previously surfaced as an uncaught "access token not found" error).

prompt:
This is a checkout of firecamp-dev/firecamp (https://github.com/firecamp-dev/firecamp) at commit 00c9eae71e3c. Developer-first OpenSource API DevTool, Postman/Insomnia alternative.

I want to see its user interface in a desktop browser, in the state a real, established user would see it. Please get the app running locally with its main interface working and realistic data in it.

# Running it
- Follow the repo's own setup docs and tooling. Take the simplest route that shows the real app: a static production build if the front end works without a backend, otherwise the app's own server (production or dev mode).
- If it needs a database or other services, run them locally with an embedded or file-based option (SQLite, in-memory, JSON files, an embedded Postgres such as PGlite) or the app's demo/mock mode.
- Don't redesign or restyle anything. Change only what's needed to build and run it.

# Tools: use mise
Install every runtime and tool you need (node, the package manager, python, bun, ...) with mise, pinned to exact versions in a mise.toml at the repo root, so the setup can be reproduced. Match what the repo asks for (engines, .nvmrc, .tool-versions, packageManager). mise is already configured for this directory: `mise install` installs into ./.ui-capture/mise, and its shims come first on PATH, so `node`, `pnpm` and the rest resolve to the pinned versions. Don't use other copies of these tools or download runtimes by hand.

# Secrets, API keys and external services: fake them
The app must not depend on anything outside this machine, and when it runs it has no network except localhost. Wherever it expects secrets, environment variables, API keys or third-party services (hosted auth or OAuth, payment providers, email, LLM or other AI APIs, maps, storage buckets, analytics, hosted databases):
- Give the required variables placeholder values so the app starts.
- Where it actually calls the service, make the call succeed locally with realistic responses: use the app's own mock, test or offline mode if it has one; otherwise point the client at a small local stub server that start.sh also starts, or swap in a stub at the integration boundary (the API client or service module). Keep stubs out of UI code. Responses should look like what the real service returns for a real user, e.g. an AI reply that actually answers, a payment history with real-looking amounts.
- Calls the browser makes directly to outside services count too; point them at the local stub.
- For sign-in through an outside provider, create a local account or use the app's dev sign-in so you can get past it.
List every stub in app.json.

# Data: like real use
Seed it the way an established user's data would look after months of actual use: specific, plausible names and content for this kind of app; dates spread over time; a realistic mix of states (done, in progress, overdue, archived, ...); realistic volume (dozens to hundreds of records where the app revolves around records); short and long text; some messiness real data has. Start from the app's own demo or seed data if it has realistic data, and extend it if it's thin. Load data through the app's own paths (its API, import, seed scripts, or its database schema), never by hardcoding it into UI code. If the app needs an account, create one and attach the data to it. No lorem ipsum or "Test 1".

# Environment
This shell is sandboxed: you can write only inside this directory (package-manager caches already point into ./.ui-capture/cache), and the network reaches only package registries, mise's download sources and GitHub (registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, repo.yarnpkg.com, github.com, codeload.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, nodejs.org, mise.jdx.dev, mise-versions.jdx.dev, release-assets.githubusercontent.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, binaries.prisma.sh, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com). Docker isn't available. A process you start in the background can't be seen or stopped from a later command, so test servers on another port than 4406 (e.g. 5406) or in the foreground under `timeout`; anything still listening on 4406 is stopped before I check.

# When you're done, leave this in ./.ui-capture/
- app.json: {"mode": "static" or "server", "entry": "/path where the main UI opens", "login": null or {"username": "...", "email": "...", "password": "..."}, "stubs": [{"service": "what was faked", "how": "how"}], "notes": "how you set it up, what data is loaded, and the main areas of the app"}
- static mode: the production build in ./.ui-capture/out, with index.html as its entry. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server; unknown paths fall back to index.html.
- server mode: ./.ui-capture/start.sh, which starts everything the app needs (stubs included) in the foreground and serves the UI at http://localhost:4406/ (it gets PORT=4406). It runs with the same PATH and restrictions as your shell, plus no network at all except localhost, so everything must already be installed, built and seeded (or seeded by start.sh itself).
- Put any scripts you write for seeding or stubbing in ./.ui-capture/ too; they're kept with the setup record.

# Order of work
You have 90 minutes in total, and anything unfinished when time runs out is lost. So work in this order:
1. Get the app building and running with its stubs, and write the contract above (app.json plus out/ or start.sh), even if it has only a little data so far.
2. Then build out the data, re-running your seed and checking the app still loads after each substantial step, so that a working state with the data loaded so far is always in place.
Write large data sets with a short generator script rather than as one long literal file.

I'll open it at 1440×900.
